cell_type_model: HEK293T cells expressing IGFLR1; recombinant human IGFL3 and IGFLR1-Fc
assay_or_perturbation: Protein-array screening and surface-plasmon-resonance binding of recombinant IGFL3 to IGFLR1 ectodomain; receptor-transfectant specificity controls
relation_type: Direct IGFL3-IGFLR1 ligand-receptor binding; IGFLR1 is a TNFR-like receptor with a predicted death-domain cytoplasmic region
pathway_branch: IGFL3-IGFLR1 extracellular binding and putative TNFR-family branch
limitations: The primary study establishes subnanomolar recombinant binding but does not define a ligand-triggered intracellular relay or cellular output for IGFL3; the cytoplasmic function of IGFLR1 remained untested.

cell_type_model: Purified human Ihh-N and BOC FNIII domain expressed in bacterial systems
assay_or_perturbation: X-ray crystal structure and biochemical binding/thermodynamic measurements of Ihh-N-BOC FNIII complex
relation_type: Direct Ihh-BOC coreceptor binding
pathway_branch: Hedgehog coreceptor ligand capture and presentation to PTCH1
limitations: The direct IHH-BOC interface is resolved, but the cited structural work does not by itself establish an IHH-specific BOC-to-PTCH1 relay or downstream cellular output.

cell_type_model: Purified human Ihh-N and CDO FNIII domain expressed in bacterial systems
assay_or_perturbation: X-ray crystal structure and biochemical binding/thermodynamic measurements of Ihh-N-CDO FNIII complex
relation_type: Direct Ihh-CDO coreceptor binding
pathway_branch: Hedgehog coreceptor ligand capture and presentation to PTCH1
limitations: The direct IHH-CDO interface is resolved, but a complete native IHH-CDO-PTCH1-SMO signaling assembly was not selectively reconstituted in this study.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human/mouse Hedgehog N-terminal domains and HHIP extracellular fragments; developmental Hedgehog models
assay_or_perturbation: Biochemical Hedgehog-HHIP binding, structural comparison of Hh-binding interfaces, and HHIP-mediated pathway inhibition/sequestration
relation_type: Direct Ihh-HHIP antagonist binding; HHIP competes with productive PTCH1 reception
pathway_branch: HHIP extracellular sequestration and inhibition of Hedgehog-PTCH1-SMO signaling
limitations: The strongest structural and functional mechanistic work centers on SHH, while IHH recognition is supported by conserved mammalian-Hh binding and comparator assays; HHIP is an antagonist, not an activating relay receptor.

cell_type_model: Ptch1-null and Ptch1-rescued cells; mouse limb/cartilage explants and embryonic skeletal models
assay_or_perturbation: Ihh or palmitoylated Ihh-N stimulation; PTCH1 binding, Ptch1 inactivation/conditional perturbation, Hedgehog reporter and Gli/Ptch target-gene assays
relation_type: Receptor-complex/pathway edge: Ihh binds PTCH1 and PTCH1 regulates SMO-dependent Hedgehog transduction
pathway_branch: Ihh-PTCH1-SMO to GLI-dependent Hedgehog transcription and chondrocyte patterning
limitations: PTCH1 is the ligand-binding receptor and SMO is the downstream transmembrane relay component; the queued composite does not imply a direct Ihh-SMO molecular contact and no terminal GLI assignment is made here.

cell_type_model: Purified human IL-11/IL-11RA/gp130 systems; Jak-deficient cells; primary human CD4 T cells; gp130-deficient HEK293 reporter cells
assay_or_perturbation: IL-11 receptor-complex assembly, coprecipitation, receptor-mutant and Jak-deficient assays, phospho-STAT3/nuclear-translocation readouts, and STAT3 reporter activation
relation_type: IL-11 engages IL11RA1 and gp130/IL6ST to activate receptor-proximal JAK/STAT signaling
pathway_branch: IL-11-IL11RA1-IL6ST-gp130-JAK1/JAK2-STAT3 inflammatory and epithelial/tumor-response branch
limitations: Classic and trans-signaling contexts differ; the strongest receptor-complex studies use soluble or reconstituted systems, and downstream outputs vary by cell type. The terminal STAT3 entry is a provisional endpoint for Module22A validation.

cell_type_model: Human T and NK lymphocytes; primary PBMCs and IL-12R mutant subjects; murine and human Th1/NK comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: IL-12 stimulation, IL12RB2 mutation or loss-of-function, JAK2/TYK2 and phospho-STAT4 assays, STAT4 DNA-binding and IFN-gamma/Th1 readouts
relation_type: IL-12 heterodimer engages the IL12RB1/IL12RB2 receptor complex and activates the JAK/STAT4 relay
pathway_branch: IL-12-p35/p40-IL12RB1/IL12RB2-JAK2/TYK2-STAT4-Th1/IFN-gamma branch
limitations: The pair denotes the heterodimeric IL-12 ligand and heteromeric receptor; shared p40/IL12RB1 biology with IL-23 is not transferred to this row. STAT4 is recorded as a provisional endpoint for Module22A validation.

cell_type_model: IL12RB1/IL23R-reconstituted Ba/F3 and NK-cell systems; human and mouse CD4 T-cell/CNS-autoimmunity models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-23 receptor reconstitution, receptor-chain blockade or variant perturbation, JAK2/TYK2 and phospho-STAT3/STAT4 assays, encephalitogenic T-cell function
relation_type: IL-23 heterodimer engages IL12RB1 with IL23R and activates a JAK/STAT receptor-proximal relay
pathway_branch: IL-23-p19/p40-IL12RB1/IL23R-JAK2/TYK2-STAT3/STAT4-Th17/CNS-inflammatory branch
limitations: IL-23 and IL-12 share p40 and IL12RB1 but use different ligand-specific receptor chains; relative STAT3 versus STAT4 usage is cell-state dependent. Both are retained as provisional Module22A endpoints.

cell_type_model: Mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages and fibroblasts; human airway smooth-muscle cells and monocyte/macrophage systems
assay_or_perturbation: IL-13 stimulation with Il13ra1 or Il4ra blockade/knockout, phospho-STAT6/STAT6 EMSA, eotaxin and alternative-macrophage gene/function assays
relation_type: IL-13 activates the type-II IL4RA/IL13RA1 receptor complex and its JAK/STAT6 relay
pathway_branch: IL-13-IL4RA/IL13RA1-JAK1/JAK2-STAT6-airway and alternative-macrophage branch
limitations: The type-II complex is exact for this row, but receptor abundance and cellular outputs differ across macrophage, fibroblast, and airway models; IL13RA2 is a separate decoy branch. STAT6 is a provisional endpoint.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-13 and IL13RA1-containing receptor systems; human monocyte/macrophage and mouse knockout models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-13 binding/receptor-chain perturbation and receptor-response comparison with IL4RA-containing complexes
relation_type: IL13RA1 is a ligand-binding/signaling-receptor component for IL-13 but is not a complete signaling receptor as an isolated subunit
pathway_branch: IL-13-IL13RA1 component of the type-II IL4RA/IL13RA1 complex
limitations: STAT6 and cellular outputs were demonstrated for IL13RA1-containing receptor complexes, not for isolated IL13RA1; no direct isolated-subunit relay or terminal endpoint is assigned.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human IL-15 receptor assemblies; IL-15 trans-presentation systems; mouse NK/CD8 tumor models; primary human CD4 T cells
assay_or_perturbation: Structural/receptor-complex assembly, trans-presentation, common-gamma-chain perturbation, phospho-STAT5 and STAT5 promoter-binding assays, NK/CD8 and CD4 functional outputs
relation_type: IL-15 engages IL15RA and the IL2RB/IL2RG signaling receptor assembly to activate JAK/STAT5
pathway_branch: IL-15-IL15RA/IL2RB/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT5-NK/CD8/T-cell branch
limitations: IL-15 trans-presentation and soluble cis-signaling have distinct receptor geometry; IL15RA is a presenting/binding subunit and IL2RB/IL2RG carry the principal signaling relay. STAT5 is provisional.

cell_type_model: Human and mouse CD4-positive T cells, including Th1 cells and CCR5-null comparator T cells
assay_or_perturbation: IL-16 binding to CD4, CD4/CCR5 association and blocking/deficiency experiments, transwell migration and ligand-binding assays
relation_type: Direct IL-16-CD4 binding with a CD4-dependent migratory cellular output; no specific intracellular relay was resolved for isolated CD4
pathway_branch: IL-16-CD4 chemotaxis with CCR5-dependent enhancement in Th1-cell recruitment
limitations: The study supports CD4 binding and migration, with CCR5 increasing the response without binding IL-16 itself; the downstream adaptor/kinase sequence remains unresolved and no terminal TF is assigned.

cell_type_model: Reconstituted human IL-17 receptor systems; IL17RC-deficient fibroblasts; epithelial and mucosal infection models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-17A/F heterodimer stimulation, IL17RA/IL17RC blockade or deletion, ACT1 co-immunoprecipitation, receptor-complex structural and inflammatory target-gene assays
relation_type: IL-17A/F activates the IL17RA/IL17RC receptor complex and recruits ACT1
pathway_branch: IL-17A/F-IL17RA/IL17RC-ACT1-SEFIR-TRAF6/TAK1-IKK/MAPK-inflammatory branch
limitations: The heterodimer-specific contribution can be confounded by coexisting IL-17A or IL-17F homodimers and receptor stoichiometry; no SCI receiver model or terminal TF endpoint is assigned.

cell_type_model: Primary human monocyte-derived macrophages; mouse NK cells and IL18R-deficient transfer/infection models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-18 stimulation, IL18R1/IL18RAP expression or loss-of-function, MyD88 dependence, MAPK/NF-kB/PI3K readouts, and NK-cell expansion assays
relation_type: IL-18 binds IL18R1 and recruits IL18RAP to form a MyD88-dependent signaling complex
pathway_branch: IL-18-IL18R1/IL18RAP-MyD88-IRAK/TRAF6-MAPK/NF-kB innate and NK-cell branch
limitations: The primary human MDM study emphasizes IL18RAP-dependent amplification of autocrine IL-18, while the NK model is infection-context dependent; a terminal TF was not promoted.

cell_type_model: Primary human monocyte-derived macrophages; mouse NK cells and IL18R-deficient transfer/infection models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-18 stimulation, IL18R1/IL18RAP expression or loss-of-function, MyD88 dependence, MAPK/NF-kB/PI3K readouts, and NK-cell expansion assays
relation_type: IL-18 binds IL18R1 and recruits IL18RAP to form a MyD88-dependent signaling complex
pathway_branch: IL-18-IL18R1/IL18RAP-MyD88-IRAK/TRAF6-MAPK/NF-kB innate and NK-cell branch
limitations: This uppercase receptor label is retained exactly as submitted and maps to the same IL18R1/IL18RAP complex; the evidence does not support treating the accessory chain as an autonomous receptor.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-1alpha/IL-1R2/IL-1RAP systems; soluble and membrane IL-1R2 decoy-receptor models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-1alpha binding and IL1R2/IL1RAP complex or decoy assays; comparison with signaling IL1R1/IL1RAP receptor complex
relation_type: IL1R2 binds IL-1alpha and can recruit IL1RAP but lacks a cytoplasmic TIR domain, producing decoy/inhibitory receptor-complex behavior
pathway_branch: IL-1alpha-IL1R2/IL1RAP decoy sequestration and blockade of IL1R1 signaling
limitations: IL1R2 is not a signaling receptor; IL1RAP recruitment does not convert the complex into a productive relay. Canonical IL1R1/IL1RAP signaling was not transferred to this exact pair.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-1beta/IL-1R2/IL-1RAP systems; soluble and membrane IL-1R2 decoy-receptor models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-1beta binding and IL1R2/IL1RAP decoy assays; competition with IL1R1/IL1RAP signaling complexes
relation_type: IL1R2 binds IL-1beta and can recruit IL1RAP but lacks a cytoplasmic TIR domain, producing decoy/inhibitory receptor-complex behavior
pathway_branch: IL-1beta-IL1R2/IL1RAP decoy sequestration and blockade of IL1R1 signaling
limitations: IL1R2 is not a signaling receptor; IL1RAP recruitment does not establish MyD88/IRAK activation for this row. Canonical IL1R1/IL1RAP signaling was not transferred.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-36Ra/IL1RL2/IL1RAP systems; keratinocyte and mouse skin inflammation models
assay_or_perturbation: Surface-plasmon-resonance and receptor-complex assays; IL-36Ra competition with IL-36 agonists and inhibition of IL1RL2-IL1RAP assembly
relation_type: IL-36Ra/IL1F5 binds IL1RL2 and prevents productive IL1RAP recruitment, acting as an antagonist rather than an activating relay
pathway_branch: IL-36Ra-IL1RL2/IL1RAP competitive inhibition of IL-36 agonist signaling
limitations: IL-36Ra has direct receptor binding and antagonist activity but does not activate the receptor-proximal MyD88 relay; processing and agonist/antagonist ratios affect potency.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-36alpha/IL1RL2/IL1RAP systems; primary human keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts; mouse skin models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-36alpha stimulation, SPR receptor binding, IL1RL2/IL1RAP recruitment, receptor blockade, NF-kB/MAPK reporter and inflammatory cytokine assays
relation_type: IL-36alpha/IL1F6 binds IL1RL2 and recruits IL1RAP to form a productive IL-36 receptor complex
pathway_branch: IL-36alpha-IL1RL2/IL1RAP-MyD88-IRAK/TRAF6-MAPK/NF-kB-epithelial inflammatory branch
limitations: IL-36 agonists require appropriate N-terminal processing for maximal activity and the strongest functional models are epithelial/inflammatory; no terminal TF endpoint is assigned.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-36gamma/IL1RL2/IL1RAP systems; primary human keratinocytes and epithelial infection models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-36gamma receptor-binding and antagonist competition, IL1RL2/IL1RAP complex assays, receptor blockade, inflammatory-gene and cytokine readouts
relation_type: IL-36gamma/IL1F8 binds IL1RL2 and recruits IL1RAP to activate the IL-36 receptor complex
pathway_branch: IL-36gamma-IL1RL2/IL1RAP-MyD88-IRAK/TRAF6-MAPK/NF-kB epithelial antimicrobial/inflammatory branch
limitations: The direct binding landscape is strongest in recombinant receptor assays and the cellular work is epithelial/infection-context dependent; no terminal TF endpoint is assigned.

cell_type_model: Recombinant IL-36beta/IL1RL2/IL1RAP systems; primary human keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts; mouse skin models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-36beta receptor binding, IL1RL2/IL1RAP recruitment, antagonist competition, receptor blockade and inflammatory-response assays
relation_type: IL-36beta/IL1F9 binds IL1RL2 and recruits IL1RAP to activate the IL-36 receptor complex
pathway_branch: IL-36beta-IL1RL2/IL1RAP-MyD88-IRAK/TRAF6-MAPK/NF-kB epithelial inflammatory branch
limitations: IL-36beta activity depends on ligand processing and receptor presentation; cellular outputs are context-specific and no terminal TF endpoint is assigned.

cell_type_model: Purified/reconstituted IL-2 receptor systems; murine HT-2 chimeric-receptor cells; human peripheral-blood T lymphoblasts
assay_or_perturbation: Stepwise IL-2 receptor assembly, IL2RB/IL2RG chimeric-receptor signaling, phospho-STAT5/DNA-binding assays and IL-2-responsive enhancer/promoter assays
relation_type: IL-2 engages the high-affinity IL2RA/IL2RB/IL2RG receptor complex and activates the JAK/STAT5 relay
pathway_branch: IL-2-IL2RA/IL2RB/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT5-T-cell proliferation and IL2RA transcription branch
limitations: The receptor has stepwise affinity states and IL2RA is a ligand-presenting chain; IL2RB/IL2RG carry the core signaling activity. STAT5 is a provisional Module22A endpoint.

cell_type_model: Murine IL2RB/IL2RG chimeric-receptor cells; human IL-2-responsive T-cell lines and lymphocytes
assay_or_perturbation: IL-2 or erythropoietin-chimera stimulation, IL2RB cytoplasmic-tail mutagenesis, STAT5 DNA-binding and STAT1/STAT3/STAT5 association assays
relation_type: IL2RB/IL2RG is the intermediate-affinity signaling receptor for IL-2 and activates a JAK/STAT relay without requiring IL2RA for signal transduction
pathway_branch: IL-2-IL2RB/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT5 with ancillary STAT1/STAT3 T-cell branch
limitations: This row intentionally omits IL2RA and therefore represents the signaling-competent intermediate-affinity receptor rather than the high-affinity trimer; STAT5 is the best-supported provisional endpoint.

cell_type_model: Primary human trabecular-meshwork cells and dermal fibroblasts; mouse keratinocytes and MRSA-skin infection models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-20 stimulation, IL20RB/IL22RA1 proximity and loss-of-function assays, phospho-STAT1/3/5 measurements, receptor perturbation and epithelial functional outputs
relation_type: IL-20 activates the type-II IL22RA1/IL20RB receptor complex and a JAK/STAT relay
pathway_branch: IL-20-IL22RA1/IL20RB-JAK1/TYK2-STAT1/STAT3 epithelial barrier, antimicrobial and inflammatory branch
limitations: IL-20 also uses the type-I IL20RA/IL20RB complex; receptor usage and STAT1/3/5 outputs vary by cell type. STAT3 is retained as a provisional endpoint only for the documented receptor-proximal pathway.

cell_type_model: Human and mouse CD4 T-cell differentiation models; human B cells/lymphoblastoid cells and acute LCMV memory-CD8 models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-21 stimulation with IL21R/IL2RG or JAK3-deficiency comparisons, phospho-STAT1/3/5 assays, STAT3-dependent gene/function and memory-cell readouts
relation_type: IL-21 engages the IL21R/IL2RG common-gamma receptor complex and activates a JAK1/JAK3-STAT relay dominated by STAT3
pathway_branch: IL-21-IL21R/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT3-Th17, B-cell differentiation and memory-CD8 branch
limitations: IL-21 can activate STAT1 and weaker STAT5 in addition to STAT3, and outputs depend strongly on lymphocyte state; STAT3 is a provisional endpoint rather than a claim that other STATs are absent.
